problem: The point $P$ has polar coordinates $(6,{45}^{∘}).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Coordinates of a Point Given in Polar Coordinates
examples.problem: The point $P$ has polar coordinates $\left( 6,\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P.$
examples.worked_solution:
To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x = r\cos\theta, \qquad y=r\sin\theta.
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
		x &= r\cos\theta\[5pt]
		 &= 6 \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)\[5pt]
		 &= 6 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\[5pt]
		 &= 3
	}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
		y &= r\sin\theta\[5pt]
		 &= 6 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)\[5pt]
		 &= 6 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\[5pt]
		 &= 3\sqrt{3}
	}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $\left(3, 3\sqrt{3}\right).$
